name: Pest season length vs average
title: Pest season length: {city} vs average
alt: Chart comparing the frost-free season in {city}, {SS} with the state average. {summary}
captions: The frost-free season in {city} runs {self_value} — the stretch between the average last spring freeze and the average first autumn freeze. Every frost-free day is a day insects can breed, so that window sets how many generations a population gets through.
{city}, {SS} gets {self_value} between freezes. Pest activity starts when the last freeze passes and ends when the first one arrives; that gap is the season a treatment plan has to cover.
At {self_value} frost-free, that is how much of the calendar pest pressure in {city} actually spans — and why a single visit rarely holds for a full year.

extras.note: Average date of the last spring freeze, 32F, 50% probability.
Average date of the first autumn freeze, 32F, 50% probability.
Degree-day accumulation base 50F — the measure insect development tracks.
Nights a year at or below 50F — the threshold MSU Extension names for mosquito activity.

_note: Benchmark removed. frost_free_state_avg had no retrievable source: NOAA publishes no statewide frost-free product, and Climate at a Glance covers temperature and precipitation only. Leaving the old AI value in place meant the chart cited NOAA for a figure nobody retrieved. A computed state average (mean of ANN-TMIN-PRBGSL-T32FP50 across in-state stations) is possible but would be our own computation, so it needs deciding on, not assuming.
